note: Qualitative agronomy rules only: no yields, prices or water volumes are stated. Every rule lists the source(s) it comes from. Sources were checked on 2026-11-14; re-check wording before publishing.

fao_sorghum.citation: FAO Land & Water, Crop information: Sorghum
fao_sorghum.supports: Sorghum is described as relatively more drought-resistant than many other crops, e.g. maize.

hadebe_sorghum.citation: Hadebe, Modi & Mabhaudhi. Drought Tolerance and Water Use of Cereal Crops: A Focus on Sorghum as a Food Security Crop in Sub-Saharan Africa (record in FAO AGRIS)
hadebe_sorghum.supports: Sorghum has high and stable water-use efficiency and drought and heat tolerance; suggested for water-scarce arid and semi-arid zones.

un_millets.citation: UN News, Millets prove tasty solution to climate and food security challenges
un_millets.supports: Millets can grow under drought and non-irrigated conditions and have a low water footprint compared with wheat, rice or maize.

preventionweb_drought_crops.citation: PreventionWeb news article on drought-tolerant crops and methods (lists cowpea and chickpea). Author, title and date were not captured in the source check: add them before publishing
preventionweb_drought_crops.supports: Cowpea and chickpea are described as drought-tolerant grain legumes.

sare_building_soils.citation: SARE, Building Soils for Better Crops, Ch. 10 Cover Crops (Magdoff & van Es)
sare_building_soils.supports: Legume cover crops (e.g. hairy vetch, red clover) fix nitrogen with Rhizobium bacteria; cover crops enhance soil health in several ways.

sare_mcp_fertility.citation: SARE, Managing Cover Crops Profitably, Building Soil Fertility (Sarrantonio)
sare_mcp_fertility.supports: Cover crops catch nutrients before they leach; legumes add nitrogen to the soil.

nrcs_340.citation: USDA NRCS, Conservation Practice Standard: Cover Crop (Code 340)
nrcs_340.supports: Cover crops are grasses, legumes and forbs planted for seasonal vegetative cover to protect and improve soil; the standard also covers planning termination to prepare the field for the next crop and to optimise soil moisture.

lower_water_rules.statement: Sorghum is a drought-resistant cereal that can replace or alternate with a more water-demanding cereal.
Millets tolerate drought and have a low water footprint compared with wheat and maize.
Cowpea and chickpea are drought-tolerant grain legumes that can be added to a rotation.

soil_restoration_rules.statement: Legume cover crops fix atmospheric nitrogen and add it to the soil, which can reduce later nitrogen fertiliser needs.
Cover crops protect and improve soil during periods when cropland would otherwise be bare.
Cover crop termination should be planned to prepare the field for the next crop and to manage soil moisture.
